answer_raw:
Copenhagen is currently ranked as the world's most liveable city according to the EIU Global Liveability Index 2026 [1][5].

The top rankings depend entirely on which index you consult, as they measure different metrics:

**EIU Global Liveability Index 2026** — per EIU, **Copenhagen** is #1 with a score of 98/100, followed by **Vienna** and **Melbourne** [1][5]. This index measures stability, healthcare, education, infrastructure, and culture [5]. While Western Europe remains a strong region, its average score has stagnated while Asia's has risen; there are now nine Asian cities in the top sittings and seven European cities [2].

**Global Cities Index 2026** — according to Oxford Economics, **New York** takes the #1 spot in their overall index [4]. This ranking uses five categories—economics, human capital, environment, and quality of life—to rank 1,000 cities [4]. While the US has eight cities in the top 20 for this index, only one US city made the cut when highlighting quality of life specifically [4].

**Numbeo Quality of Life Index 2026 Mid-Year** — reports list **Sydney, Australia** at the top for its mid-year index [8].

**Mercer Quality of Living Survey** — while the 2024 data provided lists the top 10, the specific names of the top cities are not visible in what I found to confirm the leader [3].
